summary:
ASTRA (Autonomous Astronaut Health Monitoring and Decision Support System) is a project developed to monitor astronauts' health and safety during space missions. It provides a centralized platform where astronauts and medical officers can access important health and mission-related information through separate portals with role-based access.

The system monitors various health parameters, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2), body temperature and respiratory rate. It also tracks environmental conditions such as oxygen and carbon dioxide levels, humidity, temperature and cabin pressure. In addition, ASTRA includes radiation monitoring to track personal exposure and radiation levels in the surrounding environment. A rule-based alert system identifies measurements that exceed predefined limits and notifies medical officers so they can review the situation and take appropriate action.

The application also provides features for viewing historical records, monitoring crew health, analysing measurements through graphical representations and generating reports. Developed using Python, Flask, SQLite, HTML, CSS and JavaScript, ASTRA follows an offline-first approach, allowing data to be stored and accessed even when internet connectivity is limited. The main aim of this project is to make astronaut health monitoring more organized and accessible while helping medical officers identify potential health and environmental risks during space missions.
details:
ASTRA (Autonomous Astronaut Health Monitoring and Decision Support System) is a project developed to help monitor astronauts' health and safety during space missions. Since astronauts work in an environment where even small changes in health or surroundings can become serious, the project aims to bring important monitoring information together in one place.

The system has separate portals for astronauts and medical officers. It monitors health parameters such as heart rate, blood oxygen level (SpO2), body temperature and respiratory rate. It also tracks environmental conditions, including oxygen and carbon dioxide levels, humidity, temperature and cabin pressure, along with radiation exposure. When a recorded value crosses a predefined threshold, the system generates an alert so that medical officers can review the situation. Users can also view historical records, analyse data through graphs, monitor crew health and generate reports.

The main benefit of ASTRA is that it makes health and environmental information easier to access and manage. It can help medical officers identify unusual changes early and make better-informed decisions. The project follows an offline-first approach, allowing data to be stored and accessed even with limited internet connectivity.

ASTRA was developed using Python, Flask, SQLite, HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Chart.js for data visualization. Its creative aspect lies in combining astronaut health monitoring, environmental monitoring, radiation tracking and alert management into a single platform. During development, factors such as data accuracy, security, ease of use, accessibility, reliability and limited connectivity were considered. The overall aim is to contribute towards safer and more organized health monitoring during space missions.
